reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Approval of certificate of organization by director
headings.reviewNote: Director may approve certificate of organization if conforming with chapter and bylaws and field of operation is favorable.

headings.title: Issuance and distribution of triplicate certificate of approval
headings.reviewNote: Director issues triplicate certificate of approval annexed to organization certificate and bylaws for division, credit union, and secretary of state.

headings.title: Creation of corporate entity upon issuance
headings.reviewNote: Organizers become created as a corporation under name in certificate of organization upon approval issuance.

headings.title: Organization fee payable to director of revenue
headings.reviewNote: Organization fee of five dollars payable to director of revenue at time certificate is issued.

headings.title: Provisional certificate, examinations, and revocation or merger
headings.reviewNote: Certificate is provisional with six-month and one-year examinations; director may revoke charter, dissolve, or merge credit union if standards not met.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and history (effective 6-11-85); certificate approval, triplicate filing, $5 fee, and provisional charter examinations verified.

headings.title: Creation of Credit Union Commission
headings.reviewNote: Creates Credit Union Commission within division of credit unions with statutory powers and duties.

headings.title: Commission composition and member qualifications
headings.reviewNote: Seven resident members appointed by governor with senate consent; requires bar member, four credit union representatives, two lay members, and party limit.

headings.title: Staggered commissioner terms, vacancies, and officers
headings.reviewNote: Sets staggered initial commissioner terms effective March 25, 2005, subsequent six-year terms, vacancy procedures, and selection of chair and secretary.

headings.title: Per diem compensation and expense reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Commissioners receive one hundred dollars per day while discharging duties plus actual and necessary expenses incurred.

headings.title: Quorum requirements and call of commission meetings
headings.reviewNote: Majority constitutes quorum; meetings called by chair, division director, or three members, and may meet anywhere in state.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and history (1998, 2002); Credit Union Commission creation, composition/definition, March 25, 2005 staggered terms, $100 per diem, and quorum verified.

headings.title: Appeal perfection, record review, and costs
headings.reviewNote: Notice of appeal within fifteen days of director decision; commission reviews record as in equity, takes new evidence, and assesses costs.

headings.title: Rulemaking for appeal procedures and membership criteria
headings.reviewNote: Directs commission rulemaking on appeals and group-addition criteria under ch. 536; includes post-August 28, 1998 § 536.028 nonseverability and rulemaking repeal/savings clause.

headings.title: Director compliance with commission orders
headings.reviewNote: Director of division of credit unions must act in accordance with any commission order made under subdivision (2) of section 370.062.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1998 note; appeal procedures under § 370.062/ch. 536, post-August 28, 1998 § 536.028 nonseverability rulemaking clause, and director compliance verified.

headings.title: Fees and service charges on deposit accounts
headings.reviewNote: Credit unions may impose deposit account fees subject to regulations no more restrictive than federal rules; overdraft fees not deemed interest.

headings.title: Automated teller machine foreign account access fees
headings.reviewNote: Operating or sharing agreements cannot prohibit ATM owners or operators from imposing access fees or surcharges on foreign accounts.

headings.title: Definitions of automated teller machine and foreign account
headings.reviewNote: Defines automated teller machine and foreign account for purposes of section.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and history (2003–2015); deposit account fees, ATM foreign account surcharges, and definitions verified.

headings.title: Authorized securities for credit union investments
headings.reviewNote: Permits board or delegated executive/investment committee to invest in seven categories of securities, including U.S./state/local bonds, FSLIC-insured S&L accounts, credit union shares, service stocks, and director-approved securities.

headings.title: Percentage limits on single-type and stock investments
headings.reviewNote: Caps single-type security investments at 25% of capital, surplus, and reserve fund (excluding central credit union funds and U.S. obligations) and caps subdivision (6) stock investments at 5%.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and history (1965–1988); replaced both completely mismatched draft titles/notes (erroneously describing § 370.290 borrowing) with source-accurate investment securities and 25%/5% cap headings.

headings.title: Eligibility for credit union membership
headings.reviewNote: Membership consists of organizers and duly elected persons or entities subscribing to shares and paying required entrance fees.

headings.title: Membership group categories and geographic limitations
headings.reviewNote: Groups must share common occupation, association, or employer, or defined geographic area limited to county or contiguous counties without expansion by relocation.

headings.title: Immediate family eligibility and membership retention
headings.reviewNote: Eligibility based on relation restricted to immediate family or household; members may remain until voluntary withdrawal except under section 370.340.

headings.title: Creation and terms of membership shares
headings.reviewNote: Board may create membership shares of one to one hundred dollars par value representing ownership; shares cannot be pledged as loan security.

headings.title: Subordination of membership shares upon liquidation
headings.reviewNote: In liquidation, membership shares are at risk, uninsured, and subordinated to claims of all nonmembers, creditors, other shareholders, and NCUA.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and history (through 2026 H.B. 2586); membership eligibility, common-bond/NCUA 2006 5300 geographic rules, family/retention rules, and uninsured subordinated membership shares verified.

headings.title: Authority to add groups or geographic areas
headings.reviewNote: Credit union may add groups or geographic areas complying with section 370.080.2 if statutory criteria are met.

headings.title: Employer group size limit and exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Restricts employer groups to fewer than three thousand members unless single-bond unfeasible, involuntary merger, or approved transfer.

headings.title: Inclusion of underserved communities and merged areas
headings.reviewNote: Director may allow occupation, association, or employer credit union to include proximate low-income or underserved areas, or merged credit union areas.

headings.title: Application notice, comment period, and director determination
headings.reviewNote: Notice published within five days, ten-day comment period, and decision within ten days based on service ability and member income reporting data.

headings.title: Appeal of expansion decision to commission and court
headings.reviewNote: Allows aggrieved persons showing potential actual damages to appeal within 15 days under § 370.063 and then to Cole County circuit court; notes cite 2003 Mo. banc standing ruling.

headings.title: Director authority over membership amendments
headings.reviewNote: Director has authority to approve single or multiple group membership amendments subject to chapter restrictions.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text, history (1998, 2007), and 2003 Mo. banc standing annotation; group/geographic expansion, 3,000-member employer limit, underserved areas, member data reporting, and § 370.063 appeals verified.

headings.title: Preservation of membership fields existing April 1, 1998
headings.reviewNote: Credit unions retain right to continue including persons, groups, and geographic areas included or applied for as of April 1, 1998.

headings.title: Branch office county inclusion for certain 1998-2006 expansions
headings.reviewNote: Geographic credit unions granted expansions between April 1, 1998, and March 24, 2006, may include branch office counties open prior to April 15, 2007.

headings.title: Retention of valid expansions and main office area
headings.reviewNote: Consistent post-1998 expansions retained and credit union may serve county or independent city where main office is located.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and history (1998, 2007); tightened subsection 3 title; April 1, 1998 and April 15, 2007 grandfathering clauses verified.

headings.title: Utilization, withdrawal delays, and revaluation of membership shares
headings.reviewNote: Membership shares may fulfill reserves or insurer contracts; payment on demand may be delayed; mandatory revaluation upon impairment.

headings.title: Application for redemption or withdrawal of membership shares
headings.reviewNote: Member desiring to withdraw or redeem membership shares must file written application as required by board and insurer.

headings.title: Priority deductions from share balances upon withdrawal
headings.reviewNote: Share balance paid only as funds available after deducting all fees, impaired balance, notes, or member indebtedness.

headings.title: Director approval required to amend redemption procedures
headings.reviewNote: Board procedures for redemption or withdrawal of membership shares cannot be amended without written consent of director.

headings.title: Board authorization of dividends on membership shares
headings.reviewNote: Board may authorize dividends after required reserves, which may be credited to shares subject to withdrawal restrictions.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and history (effective 3-07-91); membership share reserve use, revaluation, withdrawal applications, priority deductions, consent to amend, and dividends verified.

headings.title: Creation of office of director and rulemaking authority
headings.reviewNote: Creates director within department of commerce and insurance with exclusive supervision and rulemaking authority.

headings.title: Appointment and tenure of director by governor
headings.reviewNote: Director appointed by governor with advice and consent of senate, serving at pleasure of governor.

headings.title: Office location and full-time service requirement
headings.reviewNote: Director must maintain office at Jefferson City and devote all time to official duties.

headings.title: Experience qualifications required for director
headings.reviewNote: Requires at least three years practical experience with credit union operations, regulatory agencies, or NCUA.

headings.title: Appointment of deputy director and division staff
headings.reviewNote: Director may appoint deputy director, examiners, assistant examiners, and other necessary assistants and employees.

headings.title: Payment of traveling and divisional expenses
headings.reviewNote: Actual and necessary traveling and other divisional or office expenses paid out of state treasury as provided by law.

headings.title: Qualifications required for deputy director and examiners
headings.reviewNote: Examiners and deputy director must possess qualifications required for director.

headings.title: Performance of duties and full-time service
headings.reviewNote: Appointees perform required duties and must devote all of their time to official duties.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text, history, and § 620.010 revisor's note (2008 repeal); division director creation, appointment, Jefferson City office, 3-year qualification, staff, and expenses verified.

headings.title: Confidentiality oath required of division personnel
headings.reviewNote: Director, employees, and special agents must swear under oath not to reveal credit union conditions or facts except as required by law or in court.

headings.title: Prohibited conflicts of interest and financial ties
headings.reviewNote: Division personnel who examine or make official decisions cannot be officers, directors, receive gratuities, negotiate loans, or be indebted to state credit unions.

headings.title: Subpoena and investigatory powers of director
headings.reviewNote: Director may compel document production and witness attendance under oath, with judicial enforcement subject to court rules.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 2011 note; division confidentiality oath, conflict-of-interest/indebtedness bars, and administrative subpoena powers verified.

headings.title: Exceptions to confidentiality of examination information
headings.reviewNote: Division personnel bound to secrecy except for official reports, court witness testimony, reporting to credit union, complainant findings, regulatory sharing, or board authorization.

headings.title: Judicial disclosure standard and defamation immunity
headings.reviewNote: Disclosure requires compelling reason balancing test and hearing intervention; credit union personnel immune from libel or slander for good faith communications.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 2011 note; examination secrecy exceptions, judicial compelling-reason disclosure with intervention, and defamation immunity verified.

headings.title: Supervisory fee schedule based on total assets
headings.reviewNote: Establishes semiannual supervisory fee table across five asset tiers (under $2M to $25M+), excludes inter-credit-union shares, and treats fees as prepaid expenses.

headings.title: Division of Credit Unions Fund and fee credits
headings.reviewNote: Fees credited to dedicated fund; unexpended balance carries over to reduce next year's assessments rather than lapsing to general revenue.

headings.title: Regulatory and examination expenses funded by fees
headings.reviewNote: Regular and special examination costs, salaries, commission expenses, and up to 15 percent overhead paid from fees.

headings.title: Examiner salary schedule and federal parity limit
headings.reviewNote: Director maintains salary schedule for examiners not to exceed ninety percent parity with corresponding federal positions.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text, embedded five-tier asset fee schedule table, and history; semiannual supervisory fee, § 33.080 non-lapsing fund, 15% overhead, and 90% federal examiner parity verified.

headings.title: Reports of condition to insurer and director
headings.reviewNote: Credit union must make condition reports verified by president or designee as required by federal insurer and director.

headings.title: Penalties for delinquent or incomplete reports
headings.reviewNote: Forfeiture of twenty-five dollars per day for first seven days and seventy-five dollars thereafter, unless excused by director.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and history (through 2020 S.B. 599); verified condition reports and $25/$75 daily delinquency penalties verified.

headings.title: Annual and periodic examinations of credit unions
headings.reviewNote: Director or agents examine credit unions annually with free access to records; qualifying credit unions examined at least every eighteen months.

headings.title: Subpoena and examination of witnesses under oath
headings.reviewNote: Director and agents may subpoena and examine witnesses under oath or affirmation and documents pertaining to credit union business.

headings.title: Acceptance of approved independent audit report
headings.reviewNote: Director may accept condition audit report by approved auditor in lieu of annual examination, with costs borne by credit union.

headings.title: Acceptance of federal insurer examination report
headings.reviewNote: Director may accept final examination report made by federal credit union insurer in lieu of annual examination.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and history (through 2020 S.B. 599); annual/18-month examinations, subpoena powers, and acceptance of approved audits or federal insurer exam reports verified.

headings.title: Notice of intention to revoke certificate of approval
headings.reviewNote: Director notifies credit union of intention to revoke certificate if reports or charges are delinquent for thirty days.

headings.title: Revocation of certificate after continued neglect
headings.reviewNote: Director may revoke certificate of approval if neglect or failure continues for additional fifteen days after notice.

headings.title: Notice of revocation filed with secretary of state
headings.reviewNote: Director must file notice of revocation with secretary of state upon revoking certificate of approval.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and history (through 2020 S.B. 599); 30-day delinquency notice, 15-day revocation authority, and secretary of state filing verified.

headings.title: Grounds and notice for cease and desist orders
headings.reviewNote: Director may issue proposed order and show-cause notice for unsafe practices, violations of law/rules, or threatened violations.

headings.title: Hearing procedure, subpoenas, and judicial review
headings.reviewNote: Person entitled to public hearing within ten to thirty days; subpoenas available; order reviewable in Cole County circuit court under chapter 536.

headings.title: Temporary cease and desist orders for immediate threats
headings.reviewNote: Director may issue immediately effective temporary cease and desist order to prevent insolvency or asset dissipation; court review within fifteen days.

headings.title: Civil penalty for willful violation of final order
headings.reviewNote: Willful violation of final cease and desist order carries civil penalty of up to one hundred dollars per day.

headings.title: Definition of person under section
headings.reviewNote: Defines person as singular or plural individual, credit union, partnership, corporation, association, trust, or legal entity.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and history (effective 6-11-85); cease and desist grounds, hearing/subpoena/ch. 536 review, temporary orders, $100/day penalty, and person definition verified.

headings.title: Grounds for charter suspension or taking possession
headings.reviewNote: Director may suspend charter or take possession without notice for revoked certificate, insolvency, order noncompliance, refused exam, board request, unsafe operations, or lost insurance.

headings.title: Retention of possession during liquidation or recovery
headings.reviewNote: Director retains possession until credit union resumes business or affairs are finally liquidated.

headings.title: Operation through appointed supervisory agent
headings.reviewNote: Director may operate credit union through qualified agent under director's supervision, with expenses paid from credit union funds.

headings.title: Operational powers, litigation, and meetings during possession
headings.reviewNote: Director exercises credit union powers, prosecutes and defends lawsuits, conserves property, and calls board or member meetings.

headings.title: Mandatory conveyance of records and misdemeanor penalty
headings.reviewNote: Officers must convey all books, records, and property; failure is misdemeanor punishable by fine or imprisonment.

headings.title: Examination and asset appraisal upon taking charge
headings.reviewNote: Director promptly ascertains financial condition by examination and optional asset appraisal.

headings.title: Return of possession upon safe condition
headings.reviewNote: Director returns possession, assets, and business to directors and officers if credit union can safely resume business without reorganization.

headings.title: Reorganization or merger plan formulation
headings.reviewNote: Director proposes and attempts to implement plan if reorganization, merger, or consolidation is necessary and feasible.

headings.title: Involuntary liquidation upon unfeasible reorganization
headings.reviewNote: Director issues notice of involuntary liquidation and appoints liquidating agent if safe resumption or reorganization is not feasible.

headings.title: Judicial injunction application by credit union
headings.reviewNote: Credit union with board approval may apply within thirty days to circuit court for show-cause order to enjoin director's possession.

headings.title: Discretionary authority and official immunity of director
headings.reviewNote: Powers under section are discretionary; director and personnel immune from civil or criminal liability for good faith actions or omissions.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and history (effective 3-07-91); all 11 charter suspension, possession, agent operation, misdemeanor refusal, reorganization, involuntary liquidation, 30-day injunction, and immunity subsections verified.

headings.title: Special membership meeting on reorganization plan
headings.reviewNote: Director or credit union officers call special meeting on reorganization plan with at least seven days' notice.

headings.title: Approval of reorganization plan by two-thirds vote
headings.reviewNote: Makes reorganization plan effective upon two-thirds majority of votes cast at the meeting and directs return of possession and assets to directors and officers.

headings.title: Involuntary liquidation upon rejection of reorganization
headings.reviewNote: Director may issue notice of involuntary liquidation and appoint liquidating agent if members fail to approve plan.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and history (through 2020 S.B. 599); reorganization meeting notice, two-thirds of votes cast approval (refined sub 2 note), and involuntary liquidation verified.

headings.title: Settlement of debts and claims by receiver
headings.reviewNote: Director or receiver may compromise and settle debts owing by or claims held by credit union under court authority.

headings.title: Judicial valuation of pledged accounts against loans
headings.reviewNote: Courts may determine value of pledged accounts or shares applied in reduction of member loans.

headings.title: Receipt of property and release of liens
headings.reviewNote: Permits director in charge to receive property or money owing and release securing liens (source footnote notes word 'to' appears in original rolls).

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text, 1967 note, and original-rolls footnote ('to' in sub 3); tightened subsection 3 title; receiver settlement, collateral valuation, and lien release powers verified.

headings.title: Notice of removal of director or officer
headings.reviewNote: Permits director to serve written notice of intent to remove director, officer, or participant for violations, unsafe practices, or fiduciary breach involving dishonesty or willful disregard.

headings.title: Notice of removal or industry bar for misconduct
headings.reviewNote: Director may serve notice of removal or statewide credit union ban for misconduct at another institution evidencing unfitness or dishonesty.

headings.title: Immediate suspension or prohibition pending proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Director may immediately suspend official or prohibit participation to protect credit union or members pending administrative hearing.

headings.title: Statewide prohibition on credit union service
headings.reviewNote: Removed or suspended individual barred from holding office or participating in any Missouri credit union while order is in effect.

headings.title: Director consent exception to service prohibition
headings.reviewNote: Prohibition ceases to extent director grants written consent, which director must publicly disclose; violation treated as order violation.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and history (1967, 2011); tightened subsection 1 title; officer/director removal, cross-institution misconduct bar, immediate suspension, and director written consent exception verified.

headings.title: Judicial submission of reorganization or merger plan
headings.reviewNote: Director may submit proposed credit union reorganization or merger to court for approval, modification, or disapproval.

headings.title: Advisory membership vote and court order authority
headings.reviewNote: Court may submit plan to members for advisory nonbinding vote, and may direct director to execute sale, reorganization, or merger.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1967 note; judicial submission of reorganization/merger plan and advisory member vote verified.

headings.title: Call of special membership meetings
headings.reviewNote: Special meetings held by order of board, supervisory committee, or request of ten percent of members.

headings.title: One vote per member limitation
headings.reviewNote: At all meetings, each member is entitled to but one vote.

headings.title: Proxy voting prohibition and organizational representation
headings.reviewNote: Proxy voting prohibited; member organizations represented by single authorized person; bylaws may allow mail or electronic ballots.

headings.title: Member voting powers, bylaw amendments, and contract limitations
headings.reviewNote: Members present decide matters, amend bylaws on membership/supervisory committee, and overrule board guidelines, but cannot abrogate valid contracts.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and history (through 2020 S.B. 599); special meetings, one-member-one-vote, proxy ban with mail/electronic officer ballots, and member voting powers verified.

headings.title: Election and appointment of directors and committees
headings.reviewNote: Members elect board and optional committees; board may appoint supervisory committee if authorized by bylaws.

headings.title: Appointment or election of credit committee or manager
headings.reviewNote: Credit committee appointed by board unless bylaws provide for election, or board appoints credit manager in lieu of committee.

headings.title: Terms of office and swearing of officials
headings.reviewNote: Directors, committee members, and officers must be sworn and hold office for terms provided in bylaws.

headings.title: Execution and filing of official oath with director
headings.reviewNote: Oath subscribed, certified, transmitted immediately to director, and filed and preserved in director's office.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and history (1939, 1984); board/committee election and appointment, credit manager alternative, terms, and official oath filing verified.

headings.title: Board election of officers and dual office holding
headings.reviewNote: Board elects chair, vice chair, secretary, and treasurer; designated offices of secretary and treasurer may be held by same person if bylaws allow.

headings.title: Prescription of officer duties by board
headings.reviewNote: Duties of officers prescribed by board of directors unless otherwise specified in bylaws.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and history (through 2020 S.B. 599); board election of chair/vice chair/secretary/treasurer and officer duties verified.

headings.title: General management and special duties of board
headings.reviewNote: Board manages affairs, funds, and records, acts on memberships, sets interest rates, fixes share and loan limits, and manages investments.

headings.title: Additional administrative duties of board
headings.reviewNote: Board authorizes CEO compensation, approves budget, declares dividends, fills vacancies, amends bylaws, and considers membership appeals.

headings.title: Remote meeting participation and electronic voting
headings.reviewNote: Directors may participate by telephone or electronic means with simultaneous communication; remote votes valid with identity verification procedures.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and history (through 2026 H.B. 2586); board general/special duties, administrative duties, and remote telephone/electronic meeting participation and voting verified.

headings.title: Prohibition of compensation for board and committee members
headings.reviewNote: Members of board of directors and credit or supervisory committees cannot receive compensation for board or committee service.

headings.title: Board approval required for officer and employee salaries
headings.reviewNote: No salary paid to any officer or employee except as duly approved by board of directors.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and history (1939–1982); uncompensated board/committee service and board approval of officer/employee salaries verified.

headings.title: Bylaws and board policies governing loan decisions
headings.reviewNote: Credit committee or credit manager must follow bylaws, policies, and board procedures regarding loans and advances.

headings.title: Loan application statement of purpose and security
headings.reviewNote: Loan applicant must state purpose of loan and any security offered.

headings.title: Mandatory security for loans exceeding board limit
headings.reviewNote: Security required for loans exceeding board limit; note endorsement or share assignment constitutes security.

headings.title: Loan approval vote and credit manager appointment
headings.reviewNote: Majority approval of present committee required; credit unions over $100,000 assets may appoint credit manager with monthly reporting.

headings.title: Appeal of loan decision to board of directors
headings.reviewNote: Applicant may appeal adverse decision of committee or credit manager to board of directors if provided in bylaws.

headings.title: Advance approval and annual review of credit lines
headings.reviewNote: Committee or manager may approve lines of credit in advance; annual review required; credit line expires if over 90 days delinquent.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and history (through 2020 S.B. 599); tightened subsection 6 title; credit committee/manager loan rules, security, board appeal, and 90-day delinquency credit-line expiration verified.

headings.title: Annual examination, account verification, and suspension powers
headings.reviewNote: Supervisory committee conducts annual examination, verifies accounts per federal rules, and may suspend board members or officers by majority vote.

headings.title: Notice of special meeting following suspension
headings.reviewNote: Committee must give notice within seven days of special meeting to act on suspension.

headings.title: Special meeting called for violations or unsafe practices
headings.reviewNote: Committee by majority vote may call membership meeting to consider statutory/bylaw violations or unsafe practices.

headings.title: Annual audit report and mandatory independent audit
headings.reviewNote: Committee audits finances and reports to directors; independent audit required if assets exceed one million dollars.

headings.title: Election of supervisory committee chair
headings.reviewNote: Supervisory committee elects chair from own number if bylaws so provide.

headings.title: Filling vacancies on supervisory committee
headings.reviewNote: Directs supervisory committee to fill its own vacancies until next annual meeting, or permits board appointment if bylaws so provide.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and history (through 2020 S.B. 599); supervisory committee examinations, suspensions, over-$1M independent audit, chair election, and vacancy filling (refined sub 6 note) verified.

headings.title: Definitions of credit union and trusted contact
headings.reviewNote: Defines credit union and trusted contact for purposes of member financial exploitation prevention.

headings.title: Immunity for reporting member exploitation to authorities
headings.reviewNote: Credit union may report suspected fraud or exploitation to law enforcement or protective agencies with civil immunity.

headings.title: Voluntary establishment of trusted contact program
headings.reviewNote: Credit union may voluntarily offer trusted contact program for emergencies, lost contact, suspected fraud, or dormant accounts.

headings.title: Voluntary account features with trusted contact access
headings.reviewNote: Credit union may offer accounts setting transaction limits and limited viewing access for designated trusted contacts.

headings.title: Credit union nonliability for trusted contact actions
headings.reviewNote: Credit union is not liable for actions taken by a member's trusted contact.

headings.title: Nonliability for declining interaction with trusted contact
headings.reviewNote: Credit union not liable for declining interaction when determining in good faith that contact is not acting in member's best interest.

headings.title: Qualified immunity for designated trusted contacts
headings.reviewNote: Trusted contact acting in good faith and exercising reasonable care is immune from liability.

headings.title: Withdrawal and termination of trusted contact status
headings.reviewNote: Member or trusted contact may withdraw appointment at any time subject to credit union documentation requirements.

headings.title: Broad civil immunity regarding trusted contact program
headings.reviewNote: Credit union not civilly liable for implementing or not implementing trusted contact program or related acts or omissions.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 2025 merged-bill note; all nine exploitation-reporting immunity and voluntary trusted contact program subsections verified.

headings.title: Statutory lien on member shares, accounts, and dividends
headings.reviewNote: Credit union holds lien on all shares, accounts, and dividends for any member obligation, loan, guarantee, or fee.

headings.title: Nature of lien and perfection without waiver
headings.reviewNote: Lien is separate from other security interests, deemed perfected, and permits withdrawals without waiving lien on remaining shares.

headings.title: Exemption of encumbered shares from creditor process
headings.reviewNote: Shares subject to credit union lien are exempt from garnishment or legal process by other creditors.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and history (1939–1994); statutory lien on member accounts/dividends, perfection without withdrawal waiver, and exemption from creditor garnishment verified.

headings.title: Share cancellation and debt offset upon member departure
headings.reviewNote: Credit union may cancel shares of expelled or resigning member and apply withdrawal value to member indebtedness.

headings.title: Member address update duty and quarterly fee
headings.reviewNote: Members must keep credit union informed of current address; quarterly charge permitted if member fails to do so.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and history (through 2020 S.B. 599); share cancellation/offset upon departure and member address update duty with quarterly charge verified.

headings.title: Minor share account rights, payment, and valid release
headings.reviewNote: Shares in minor's name held for exclusive benefit, payable to minor with valid release, subject to joint tenancy rules under section 370.287.

headings.title: Joint owner requirement for minor accounts
headings.reviewNote: Credit union may require parent, guardian, or responsible person to be joint owner on minor's account.

headings.title: Statutory liens, conservator payments, and transfers to minors
headings.reviewNote: Subjects minor accounts to § 370.250/consensual liens, permits payment to § 475.045 conservator, and applies §§ 404.005–404.094 transfers to minors law (original rolls read 'Transfer').

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text, history (1959, 2013), and original-rolls footnote ('Transfer'); minor share rights, joint owner option, § 370.250 liens, § 475.045 conservator discharge, and §§ 404.005–404.094 cross-reference verified.

headings.title: Trustee or custodian powers for retirement plans
headings.reviewNote: Credit union may act as trustee or custodian of individual retirement accounts, self-employed pensions, or sponsor retirement plans.

headings.title: Fiduciary powers for pension and profit sharing plans
headings.reviewNote: Credit union may act as trustee or custodian under pension and profit-sharing plans.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1984 note; trustee/custodian powers for IRAs, self-employed/sponsor retirement plans, and pension/profit-sharing plans verified.

headings.title: Joint tenancy share creation, survivorship, and member rights
headings.reviewNote: Shares issued in joint tenancy vest in survivors; nonmember joint tenants cannot vote, borrow, or hold office; valid credit union release.

headings.title: Effect of disability or incapacity of joint tenant
headings.reviewNote: Adjudication of disability does not sever joint tenancy; conservator acts on behalf of disabled joint owner.

headings.title: Spousal accounts presumed joint tenancy
headings.reviewNote: Accounts held by spouses or survivor considered joint tenancy and not tenancy by the entirety unless specified otherwise.

headings.title: Discharge upon payment, stop-payment notice, and tax immunity
headings.reviewNote: Discharges credit union upon payment prior to written stop-payment notice, exempts from state estate/succession taxes, and applies §§ 404.005–404.094 (original rolls read 'section 1' and 'Transfer').

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text, history (1959, 2013), and original-rolls footnotes ('section 1', 'Transfer'); joint tenancy survivorship, disability/conservator rule, spousal presumption, stop-payment discharge, and §§ 404.005–404.094 cross-reference verified.

headings.title: Refusal of payment during account dispute or uncertainty
headings.reviewNote: Credit union may refuse payment if uncertain of entitlement or with actual knowledge of dispute among claimants or beneficiaries.

headings.title: Written notice of payment refusal and release conditions
headings.reviewNote: Credit union must give written notice of refusal basis; withholding continues until written consent or court order.

headings.title: Immunity from damages for payment refusal
headings.reviewNote: Credit union shall not be liable for damages resulting from refusing payment under section.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 2020 note; account payment refusal during uncertainty/dispute, written notice and release conditions, and damages immunity verified.

headings.title: Interest rate limits and minimum monthly charge
headings.reviewNote: Loans permitted at reasonable interest not exceeding statewide lender maximums; minimum charge up to one dollar per month allowed.

headings.title: Authorized borrower loan expenses and fees
headings.reviewNote: Credit union may charge borrower for title examination, credit investigations, credit life insurance, and official filing fees.

headings.title: Interest refunds to members after dividend period
headings.reviewNote: Board may allocate interest receipts to refund members in proportion to interest paid, with discretion to exclude delinquent loans or specific classes.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text, history (effective 3-01-11), and Const. Art. III § 44 cross-reference; tightened subsection 3 title; interest limits, § 442.010 loan expenses, and interest refunds verified.

headings.title: Loan limits, security rules, and board policies
headings.reviewNote: Loans governed by bylaws and committee approval; maximum loan is $2,000 or ten percent of assets; unsecured loans governed by board policy.

headings.title: Loan terms for officials and reporting requirements
headings.reviewNote: Loans to directors and committee members cannot be on more favorable terms; must be reported to board next meeting and to director annually.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and history (through 2020 S.B. 599); $2,000/10%-of-assets loan limits, board unsecured policies, and director/committee loan terms and annual reporting verified.

headings.title: Loan loss reserve requirement for membership shares
headings.reviewNote: Credit unions with membership shares must maintain loan loss reserve of 100 percent of five-year average losses; director may waive.

headings.title: Contingency reserve requirement and director waiver
headings.reviewNote: Must maintain contingency reserve of at least five percent of membership shares for non-loan losses; director may waive upon application.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1984 note; 100% five-year average loan loss reserve and 5% contingency reserve for membership shares with director waiver verified.

headings.title: Expulsion of member by two-thirds membership vote
headings.reviewNote: Members by two-thirds vote of those present at regular meeting may expel any member.

headings.title: Voluntary withdrawal from membership upon request
headings.reviewNote: A member may withdraw from credit union upon request.

headings.title: Administrative expulsion under board policy and appeal rights
headings.reviewNote: Board, president, or designated executive may expel member under written board policy, with right of appeal.

headings.title: Share disbursement, dividend accrual, and sixty-day notice
headings.reviewNote: Share balance with accrued dividends paid as funds become available, subject to sixty days' notice and offset of member debts.

headings.title: Termination of member rights and retention of liability
headings.reviewNote: Withdrawing or expelled member loses rights and benefits but remains liable for outstanding obligations to credit union.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and history (through 2020 S.B. 599); two-thirds vote expulsion, voluntary withdrawal, board-policy expulsion with appeal, 60-day payout/offset, and retained liability verified.

headings.title: Voluntary dissolution vote and consent filing
headings.reviewNote: Three-fourths membership vote required to dissolve; verified consent and officer roster filed with division director.

headings.title: Director certificate of compliance with dissolution
headings.reviewNote: Director executes certificate verifying filing of consent and compliance with statutory dissolution procedures.

headings.title: Filing of dissolution certificate with secretary of state
headings.reviewNote: Director files dissolution certificate in office of secretary of state.

headings.title: Appointment of liquidating agent and liquidation procedure
headings.reviewNote: Director appoints share insurer, guarantor, or other suitable liquidating agent to liquidate credit union pursuant to rules.

headings.title: Dissolution rulemaking and final dissolution notice
headings.reviewNote: Director promulgates dissolution rules and notifies secretary of state of final dissolution upon liquidating agent's notice.

headings.title: Rulemaking compliance with section 536.024
headings.reviewNote: Rules promulgated under chapter authority effective only if compliant with section 536.024.

headings.title: Transfer of membership and field upon dissolution
headings.reviewNote: Director may transfer dissolving credit union's membership and field to consenting credit union, with member records forwarded.

headings.title: Orderly dissolution at board request following member vote
headings.reviewNote: Following member dissolution vote, director or appointee may bring about orderly liquidation at request of board.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and history (through 2020 S.B. 599); tightened subsection 7 title; three-fourths voluntary dissolution vote, director certificate, liquidating agent, § 536.024 rulemaking, and membership transfer verified.

headings.title: Merger with domestic, foreign, or federal credit unions
headings.reviewNote: Missouri credit unions may merge with other Missouri credit unions or out-of-state and federal credit unions formed for same purpose.

headings.title: Board approval and contents of merger plan
headings.reviewNote: Majority board vote approves merger plan specifying merging and surviving credit unions, terms, share conversion, and bylaw amendments.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and history (1955–1988); tightened subsection 1 title; domestic/foreign/federal merger authority and board merger plan contents verified.

headings.title: Authority to consolidate into new credit union
headings.reviewNote: Credit unions formed under Missouri, out-of-state, or federal law may consolidate into a new credit union.

headings.title: Board approval and contents of consolidation plan
headings.reviewNote: Majority board vote approves consolidation plan setting forth names, resulting entity, terms, share conversion, and new bylaws.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and history (1955–1988); consolidation authority into new credit union and board consolidation plan contents verified.

headings.title: Membership vote, meeting notice, and ballot procedures
headings.reviewNote: Board directs submission to members with 14 to 30 days' notice; mail or electronic balloting allowed; surviving board ratifies without member vote.

headings.title: Mandatory membership approval for consolidation
headings.reviewNote: In consolidation, boards of all consolidating credit unions must submit plan to members pursuant to subsection 1 procedures.

headings.title: Director waiver of membership meeting
headings.reviewNote: Permits director to waive membership meeting upon board request for financial difficulty, lost/reduced field of membership, or limited growth potential.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and history (1955–2011); tightened subsection 3 title; 14–30 day meeting notice, ballot voting, consolidation member vote, and director waiver verified.

headings.title: Majority member approval required for merger or consolidation
headings.reviewNote: Plan approved upon affirmative vote of majority of members present and voting at each credit union meeting with quorum.

headings.title: Director approval of articles of merger or consolidation
headings.reviewNote: Articles submitted to division director, who approves if in conformity with law and in best interest of majority of members.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and history (1955–1982); majority member vote with quorum and director approval of merger/consolidation articles verified.

headings.title: Execution and contents of merger or consolidation articles
headings.reviewNote: Articles executed by chair/vice chair, sealed, attested by secretary, containing plan, total membership, and vote tally.

headings.title: Director examination, filing, and certificate issuance
headings.reviewNote: Director reviews conformity, verifies fees paid, files permanent record, notifies secretary of state, and issues certificate.

headings.title: Effective date of merger or consolidation
headings.reviewNote: Merger or consolidation is legally effected upon issuance of certificate by director of division of credit unions.

headings.title: Delivery of certificate to resulting credit union
headings.reviewNote: Certificate with affixed articles returned to surviving or new credit union or its representative.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and history (through 2020 S.B. 599); tightened subsections 1 and 4 titles; execution, filing, effective date upon certificate issuance, and return of documents verified.

headings.title: Dissenting shareholder objection and fair value demand
headings.reviewNote: Shareholder objecting in writing and not voting in favor may demand book fair value within ten days of merger or consolidation.

headings.title: Contents of dissenting shareholder demand
headings.reviewNote: Written demand must state the number of shares owned by dissenting shareholder.

headings.title: Presumption of consent upon failure to demand payment
headings.reviewNote: Failure to demand payment within ten-day period creates conclusive presumption of consent to merger or consolidation.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and history (1955, 2020); dissenting shareholder written objection, 10-day book fair-value demand, share-count statement, and conclusive consent presumption verified.

headings.title: Application by foreign credit union for Missouri certificate
headings.reviewNote: Credit union organized under laws of another state may apply for Missouri certificate of organization.

headings.title: Contents required in foreign credit union application
headings.reviewNote: Application specifies name, jurisdiction, duration, Missouri office, officers, capital, surplus, and enabling information.

headings.title: Execution and verification of foreign credit union application
headings.reviewNote: Application executed by credit union chair or vice chair and verified.

headings.title: Authenticated charter, bylaws, and good standing certificate
headings.reviewNote: Application must include authenticated copies of charter, amendments, bylaws, and certificate of good standing from home jurisdiction.

headings.title: Provisional certificate, charter cancellation, and final approval
headings.reviewNote: Director issues 90-day provisional certificate; final approval issued upon proof of foreign charter cancellation under section 370.040.

headings.title: Transfer of Missouri charter to another jurisdiction
headings.reviewNote: Missouri credit union in good standing may transfer charter upon board approval, member vote, director approval, and foreign certificate.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and history (through 2020 S.B. 599); tightened subsection 6 title; foreign credit union application, 90-day provisional charter, and Missouri charter transfer verified.

headings.title: Conversion of state credit union to federal charter
headings.reviewNote: Sets state-to-federal conversion steps: board approval, 14–30 day notice, majority ballot vote, 10-day filing, 90-day federal charter filing, state cessation, and asset/obligation vesting.

headings.title: Requirements for federal to state credit union conversion
headings.reviewNote: Permits federal credit union conversion to state charter by complying with federal requirements and filing proof of compliance and certificate of organization with director.

headings.title: Director approval and asset vesting for state conversion
headings.reviewNote: Directs director approval and secretary of state filing of organization certificate, making the federal credit union a state credit union vested with all assets and obligations.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and history (through 2020 S.B. 599); fixed shifted draft headings on subsections 2–3 (erroneously continuing state-to-federal steps) to accurately cover federal-to-state conversion and director approval/asset vesting.

headings.title: Mandatory NCUSIF share insurance application and enforcement
headings.reviewNote: Requires non-NCUSIF credit unions to apply within 90 days of March 7, 1991, mandates NCUSIF coverage for new charters, permits enforcement, and protects good-faith converting credit unions.

headings.title: Twenty-four-month deadline to obtain NCUSIF insurance certificate
headings.reviewNote: Requires NCUSIF insurance certificate within 24 months of March 7, 1991 (up to 12-month director extension) or mandatory liquidation unless merged/consolidated with NCUSIF-insured credit union.

headings.title: Submission of insurance certificate copy to director
headings.reviewNote: Requires credit union to forward copy of NCUSIF certificate of insurance to director promptly and within 30 days after receipt.

headings.title: Duty to maintain NCUSIF insurance and termination consequences
headings.reviewNote: Requires maintaining NCUSIF insurance in force and directs merger, consolidation, or liquidation upon termination of NCUSIF coverage.

headings.title: Exemption for central credit unions
headings.reviewNote: Exempts central credit unions organized under § 370.365 from 'this act' (1991 H.B. 180 per asterisk note).

headings.title: Return of funds by nonfederal insurer upon conversion
headings.reviewNote: Requires nonfederal insurer to return unearned premiums, paid-in capital, and special assessments upon NCUSIF conversion absent contrary member agreement (notes cite 1993 E.D. Mo. and 1995 8th Cir. Contract Clause decisions).

headings.title: Division approval required for nonfederal insurer bylaw amendments
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits nonfederal insurer bylaw amendments from binding Missouri credit unions unless approved by division of credit unions.

headings.title: Division approval required for nonfederal insurer special assessments
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits nonfederal insurer special assessments or fees on Missouri credit unions without division of credit unions approval.

headings.title: Private excess share insurance permitted above NCUSIF coverage
headings.reviewNote: Permits nonfederal insurers to issue private excess share insurance above required basic NCUSIF coverage.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text, 1991 note (effective 3-07-91), H.B. 180 asterisk note, and 1993/1995 federal Contract Clause annotations; replaced all nine completely mismatched draft titles/notes (erroneously describing charter conversion) with source-accurate NCUSIF share insurance and nonfederal insurer headings.

headings.title: Definition of central credit union and shareholding threshold
headings.reviewNote: Central credit union organized primarily to serve other credit unions; privilege suspendable if credit union shares fall below 75 percent.

headings.title: Chartering, membership, investment, and borrowing powers
headings.reviewNote: Membership limited to credit unions/associations; may invest in credit union shares, buy loans, borrow up to 5x capital, and lend up to 25% assets.

headings.title: Examination fee cap for central credit unions
headings.reviewNote: Director charges actual and necessary examination costs, not to exceed three thousand dollars, in lieu of other fees.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and history (1977, 1978); central credit union 75% shareholding threshold, chartering/investment/5x borrowing/25% lending powers, and $3,000 exam fee cap verified.

headings.title: Central credit union conversion, consolidation, or merger authority
headings.reviewNote: Permits § 370.365 central credit union conversion, consolidation, or merger with a bank, trust company, or central credit union under §§ 370.351–370.357 with dual regulatory approvals and name restrictions.

headings.title: Finance director examination, certificate issuance, and succession
headings.reviewNote: Sets bank/trust conversion articles (including § 370.356(1) stock conversion), finance director investigation and appeal rights, county recording, and property/fiduciary succession.

headings.title: Consummation and dissenting rights in consolidation or merger
headings.reviewNote: Governs consummation of consolidation or merger under federal, §§ 370.351–370.357, and banking laws, preserves § 370.356 and bank dissenting shareholder rights, and continues corporate identity.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and history (1996, 2008); refined subsections 1 and 3 titles to cover full conversion/consolidation/merger scope, §§ 370.351–370.357 compliance, § 370.356 dissenting rights, and finance director chartering.
